clue.text: Cover a conurbation's potential

parts.note: a cap is a cover, as on a bottle or pen
a city is a large urban sprawl, a conurbation; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up how much a sprawling urban area could hold or grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity is the ability or potential to do or hold something.

clue.text: Firm food commonly sent back in Germany

parts.note: Co is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: something sent back goes the reverse way, so this word is read right to left

parts.note: grub is the colloquial, common word for food

explanation.surface: A company's food delivery is returned somewhere in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective describing the food but is a company. The definition is loose: the answer is a town found in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Coburg is a historic town in Bavaria, so it is a place located in Germany.

clue.text: Set about one on equal terms

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the group's word goes round the numeral

parts.note: a party is a set or group of people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A group arranges a contest so that everyone competes on equal terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality, being on the same footing as another.

clue.text: Clot wanting permission to go with a novice

parts.note: congé is formal leave or permission to depart
L is the learner plate sign, standing for a novice

explanation.surface: A beginner who wants leave to depart is called a clot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like an insult (a fool) but is the verb: to thicken. CONGE is congé, French-derived for leave to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: To clot is to thicken or set into a solid mass, as blood or gravy does.

clue.text: Trails the wild stag

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the deer's word run amok into a new order

explanation.surface: A hunter follows the tracks of a wild deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is to trail behind, so tags means follows or trails.

clue.text: Sacred symbol bearing a figure-a small horse

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a figure
an Arab is a breed of horse, relatively small

explanation.surface: A religious emblem depicts a little pony.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab beetle was a holy emblem in ancient Egypt, worn as an amulet.

clue.text: Calling the worker to follow a number and strike

indicators.note: to follow tells us the insect comes after the other two pieces

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, a number
to lam is to thrash or strike
the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: A union rep calls on a worker to go along with a vote and walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but gives LAM, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamant means crying out or clamouring, insistently calling for attention.

clue.text: Argued for a person getting into debt

indicators.note: getting into means the pieces go inside the debt word

parts.note: being in the red means in debt, so red stands for debt
as can mean for, in the role of
one is a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded on behalf of a person sinking into debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reasoned is to have argued logically or made a case.

clue.text: Sit the finest mount?

parts.note: best means finest
to mount a horse is to ride it

explanation.surface: Get on the best horse in the stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' reads as a noun, a horse, but supplies the verb RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to sit astride, with a leg on each side.

clue.text: The aristocracy stop on time

parts.note: a bar is a barrier that stops something
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: The nobility halts the passage of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The baronage is the whole body of barons, the nobility collectively.

clue.text: Hector has housing right as can be

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the word has encloses the other letters

explanation.surface: A bully called Hector is as right as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' looks like a man's name but is the verb, to bully. 'can be' just fills out the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or badger someone, which is what pestering persistently means.

clue.text: The young child accompanying a princess

parts.note: an infant is a very young child

explanation.surface: A little one goes along with a royal lady.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese king, a royal princess.

clue.text: The cad's devastating retort

indicators.note: devastating suggests the reply is wrecked into a new order of letters

explanation.surface: A scoundrel delivers a crushing reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is a dated British word for a cad, a dishonourable man.

clue.text: Popular pro

definitions.meaning: liked and approved of by people
for, in support of, as opposed to against

explanation.definitionFit: Being well liked is being looked on with approval, and supporting a proposal is being for it; both are that phrase.

clue.text: Shows paper's a material

indicators.note: material taken as raw stuff to be worked up, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: the possessive is read as a plural here, giving all its letters to the mix

explanation.surface: A display of paper as a material for craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' is read as an adjective meaning to be made into something, so it signals a reworking of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shows means is seen or becomes visible, the same as turning up into view.

clue.text: Tusk force!

parts.note: a pun on task force: a group of large tusked animals moving together

explanation.definitionFit: A group of tusked animals forms a herd, a force of tusks.

clue.text: Miss a point and failure could result

indicators.note: could result says these letters may produce a different arrangement

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Missing the point could end in failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like the verb, but is the title of a young unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fräulein is the German title for an unmarried woman, equivalent to Miss.

clue.text: Thinking again it might be let in for once

indicators.note: it might be hints that these letters could form something else when reshuffled

explanation.surface: Having mulled it over, someone might be admitted just this once.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means after reconsideration, having thought something over again.

clue.text: Fussy individual taking clergyman in hand

indicators.note: in means placed inside the hand word

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
a means one, a single individual
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a clergyman's degree

explanation.surface: A fussy person takes a vicar in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a noun, a person fussy about fads.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddist is someone fussy about passing crazes, especially in diet.

clue.text: Far from fresh buffet, which is unusual

parts.note: food that has gone off is far from fresh
to buffet is to strike or beat

explanation.surface: A stale buffet meal is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' suggests a spread of food but is the verb, to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Majestic direction to serve a good meal

parts.note: regal means kingly or majestic
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A royal instruction to put on a fine dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale is to entertain lavishly with food and drink.

clue.text: Approach a head of department over an opening

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the department word

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A department head is approached over a job vacancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' sounds like a vacancy but gives VENT, a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival or coming, the approach of something.

clue.text: Jumpers guys found quite unacceptable

explanation.definitionFit: Leapers spring along, and in dated British slang ill-mannered men are scoundrels; one word covers both.

clue.text: Disgust with away result

parts.note: off means away, as in 'go off'
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: Fans are disgusted at the away match outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to displease or disgust someone.

clue.text: Some excellent hotels offer only limited accommodation

indicators.note: some means only part of the words, the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A number of good hotels only have small rooms available.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery, with confined space.

clue.text: This really is nauseating stuff

parts.note: read literally, a substance made to induce vomiting, not something merely distasteful

explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a drug that causes vomiting, literally sickening stuff.

clue.text: Plug into cool music

indicators.note: into means the plug word goes inside the calm word

parts.note: serene means calm and cool
an ad is an advertisement, a plug

explanation.surface: Someone plugs into some cool music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests an electrical socket but gives AD, a promotional plug.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a piece of music, traditionally sung under a window.

clue.text: Near to collapse? Fancy that!

indicators.note: collapse suggests the letters fall apart and rebuild into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is about to fall down, which is surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy that!' reads as an exclamation; 'Fancy' is the adjective, elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is fancy.

clue.text: Most even put home before a good game of cricket

indicators.note: before places the home word ahead of the cricket match

parts.note: a flat is a home, an apartment
a Test is an international cricket match, the top form of the game

explanation.surface: Someone stays home before going to a good cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a multi-day international cricket fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattest means most level, with the fewest bumps.
